skill.name: planning-and-task-breakdown
skill.description: Turns a software specification into ordered, verifiable tasks with dependencies, acceptance criteria, checkpoints, and scope guidance.
skill.summary: Create an implementation-ready task plan from a software specification.
skill.author: addyosmani

security_audit.summary: All 28 static findings are false positives. The flagged backticks, paths, and checklist text are Markdown documentation examples, not executable commands, reconnaissance, or path traversal. No semantic security findings or prompt injection attempts were identified.

remediation.issue: Static analysis interprets Markdown backticks and fenced examples as Ruby or shell execution.
remediation.suggestion: Apply language-aware scanning that distinguishes Markdown code formatting from executable source before assigning external-command risk.

remediation.issue: Documentation links and checklist language trigger filesystem and reconnaissance patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Treat prose-only relative references and generic verification text as non-executable unless a file operation or network action is actually instructed.

content.value_statement: Large or vague software work can hide dependencies, missing acceptance criteria, and verification gaps. This skill converts a specification into ordered task slices with checkpoints, scope guidance, and clear completion conditions.
actual_capabilities: Decomposes a software specification into small, ordered implementation tasks.
Maps dependencies and recommends a bottom-up implementation order.
Creates acceptance criteria, verification steps, dependencies, and likely files for each task.
Uses vertical slicing to organize complete, testable feature paths.
Adds checkpoints, task-sizing guidance, risks, and open questions to a plan.
Explains when to use a local task list or an external issue tracker.
limitations: It produces planning guidance and documents; it does not implement or test the software.
It cannot infer missing requirements without user or repository context.
File lists, estimates, and dependencies are recommendations that require human review.
It does not manage external trackers unless another tool performs those actions.

use_cases.title: Turn a product brief into an implementation plan
use_cases.description: Convert a feature brief into ordered tasks with dependencies, acceptance criteria, verification steps, and review checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Prepare an agent-ready coding task list
use_cases.description: Break a large engineering request into focused vertical slices that an AI coding agent can implement and verify independently.
use_cases.target_user: Software engineers using Claude Code, Codex, or Claude

use_cases.title: Coordinate work across contributors
use_cases.description: Identify parallel work, shared contracts, sequencing constraints, risks, and the task-list location for a multi-person project.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple task breakdown
prompt_templates.prompt: Break this request into ordered tasks. For each task, include a short description, acceptance criteria, verification step, dependency, and estimated scope: [paste request].

prompt_templates.title: Map dependencies before implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this specification and map the dependency graph. Then propose a bottom-up task order with one checkpoint after each major phase: [paste specification].

prompt_templates.title: Plan a vertical feature slice
prompt_templates.prompt: Use vertical slicing to plan this feature. Separate foundation work from complete user flows, identify likely files, define testable acceptance criteria, and flag tasks that are too large: [describe feature and repository context].

prompt_templates.title: Review a plan for delivery risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the following implementation plan for missing dependencies, unclear acceptance criteria, oversized tasks, weak verification, unsafe parallelization, and missing checkpoints. Return a corrected ordered plan with open questions: [paste plan].

output_examples.input: Add email notifications when a user receives a comment.
output: Task 1: Define notification preferences and the comment event contract. Verify the schema and event payload with focused tests.
Task 2: Implement notification delivery for one provider. Verify successful delivery, provider failure handling, and retry behavior.
Task 3: Add the user-facing preference flow. Verify that disabled notifications are not sent.
Checkpoint: Run the focused test suite and confirm the comment-to-notification flow end to end.

output_examples.input: We need to add search with filters to an existing application.
output_examples.output: The plan separates indexing, the search API, one complete filtered user flow, and later performance work. Each task includes dependencies, acceptance criteria, verification, likely files, and a scope estimate.

best_practices: Provide the specification, repository conventions, and known constraints before requesting a plan.
Require every task to include testable acceptance criteria and a concrete verification step.
Review dependencies, checkpoints, scope estimates, and open questions before implementation begins.
anti_patterns: Ask for a plan when the change is a single obvious file edit.
Accept tasks that say only to implement a feature without acceptance criteria or verification.
Parallelize work that changes a shared contract before the contract is defined.

faq.question: What input does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide a specification, goal, constraints, and relevant repository context. More context produces more reliable dependencies and file recommendations.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: No. It creates an implementation plan and task list. A separate coding step or agent must implement and test the work.

faq.question: What is vertical slicing?
faq.answer: Vertical slicing delivers one complete, testable user flow across the needed layers instead of finishing one technical layer at a time.

faq.question: How are task dependencies handled?
faq.answer: The skill maps prerequisites and orders tasks so foundational contracts and data structures are ready before dependent work begins.

faq.question: Can the plan use an issue tracker?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explains how to map task details to an external tracker and record the tracker choice in the plan document.

faq.question: How should I review the generated plan?
faq.answer: Confirm the requirements, dependencies, acceptance criteria, verification steps, scope estimates, risks, checkpoints, and open questions before implementation.
